tasks.title: todo add appends an item and prints its id
acceptance: `todo add "buy milk"` appends {id, text, done:false, created} to the store and prints the new id.
Ids are small integers that never repeat within a store, even after removals.
A test adds two items to a temp store and asserts the ids 1 and 2 and the stored text.

tasks.title: the project owns its domain name
acceptance: `todo-cli.example` is registered for the project: a single-use card minted through the platform's card rail, within the owner's bound and merchant category, pays the registrar once, and the purchase shows on the audit trail and on this item's page with the merchant.
`docs/DOMAIN.md` records the domain, the registrar and the amount, and a test asserts the file names the domain.

tasks.title: todo list prints open items with their ids
acceptance: `todo list` prints one line per open item as `<id>  <text>`, oldest first, and `nothing to do` when empty.
A test covers both the empty store and a store with two items.

tasks.title: todo done marks an item finished
acceptance: `todo done <id>` sets done:true; `list` hides done items unless `--all`, which shows them with a `[x]` prefix.
An unknown id exits 1 with `no such item: <id>`.
Tests cover marking, hiding, --all, and the unknown id.

tasks.title: todo remove deletes an item
acceptance: `todo remove <id>` deletes the item; a later `add` does not reuse its id.
Tests cover removal and the non-reuse of ids.

tasks.title: todo list --json prints the items as JSON
acceptance: `todo list --json` prints the open items (all with --all) as a JSON array of {id, text, done, created}.
A test parses the output and checks the shape.

tasks.title: items can carry a due date
acceptance: `todo add "pay rent" --due 2026-10-01` stores due as an ISO date; `list` shows `(due 2026-10-01)` and sorts due items first by date.
Overdue items (due before today) show `OVERDUE` in `list`; a test pins today with $TODO_TODAY.

tasks.title: todo stats counts the store
acceptance: `todo stats` prints `open <n>  done <n>  overdue <n>` and a test asserts the counts on a seeded store.

tasks.title: the README's usage section is the help text
acceptance: README.md contains a `## Usage` section whose fenced block equals `todo --help` output, and a test asserts they match.
